👋 Hi! Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.

💬 Join our developer Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai to discuss your PR in `#pr-reviews`, coordinate on features in `#feat-` channels, or join special interest groups in `#sig-` channels.

PRs do not trigger a full CI run by default. Once the PR is approved and ready to go, your PR reviewer(s) can run CI to test the changes comprehensively before merging.

To run CI, PR reviewers can either: Add `ready` label to the PR or enable auto-merge.

If you have any questions, please reach out to us on Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai.

body: Oh, does this still depend on an AITER bump, @mjkvaak-amd? I thought that this should be merged, but then I started thinking about that.

I found a bug in the fusion pass of RMSNorm with 3D layout + `quant_fp8`  and force-pushed the change on the branch: the two previous commits are replaced by a single one, `e0ae89d`. 

**Changes:**
* `_output_projection` now normalises on the per-head `(N, H, D)` tensors as the callers already pass them, and flattens once for `out_proj`. All four of `forward_hip`, `forward_cuda`, `forward_xpu` and `forward_cpu` allocate that shape already.

* When `quant_fp8` is decomposed rather than run as a custom op, the quant's group reshape back to `(N, H, D)` is a no-op that the compiler drops. That configuration now gets its own pattern variant, traced with `remove_noop_reshapes` stripping the reshape ops.

* `test_aiter_fusion_rmsnorm_gated_quant` scope expanded and is now parametrized over both per-head layouts and both `quant_fp8` modes. In my earlier commit the four `(N, H, D)` cases fail: the two `+quant_fp8` ones raise `InductorError`, the two `-quant_fp8` ones match zero patterns. Suite is 75 passed, 24 skipped. 

The trace, serving sweep and GSM8K results in the description are unchanged and still describe this code

@dllehr-amd apologies for invalidating the CI run on `2ec6d92` — please re-trigger whenever convenient. Would be great if you can also remove the stale labels from my bad rebase in August (`rust`, `cohere`, `multi-modality`, `kv-connector` and friends could be dropped); I can't remove them myself.

> Oh, does this still depend on an AITER bump, @mjkvaak-amd? I thought that this should be merged, but then I started thinking about that.

No AITER bump is needed. I marked this a draft, because I found a problem with RMSNorm and `quant_fp8` fusion that I hadn't previously thought of: the details of this are in my answer to Doug above. It's now fixed and I reopened the PR for review.
/ci run

✅ @mjkvaak-amd, CI is now available for this PR.

- `/ci run` starts upstream CI; `/amd-ci run` starts AMD CI only.
- Your branch must contain every commit currently on its upstream target branch. Merge or rebase onto the latest target branch, then rerun the command. Append `--allow-stale` to a run command to test an outdated branch at your own risk.
- `/ci retry` retries failed jobs in the CI build for the current PR head. If the current head has no CI build, it starts a new CI build for the current head containing only jobs that failed in the latest earlier CI build for this PR.
- `/amd-ci retry` retries failed jobs in AMD CI for the current PR head. Use `/amd-ci run` when the current head has no AMD CI build.
- `/ci cancel` cancels scheduled or running CI builds for this PR branch; `/amd-ci cancel` does the same for AMD CI only.
